**Sūrat al-Naḥl** (The Bee)

Makkan (*Makkiyyah*, revealed in Makkah) [one hundred and twenty-eight verses] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]], except His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of what you were made to suffer﴾ to the end of the surah [[Mujahid, ʿAṭiyyah, and Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is entirely Makkan, and this is also related from al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah, and ʿAṭāʾ. Ibn ʿAbbas said in one narration: it is Makkan except the verse "And if you retaliate..." (16:126), which was revealed after the killing of Ḥamzah. He said in another narration: it is Makkan except for three verses revealed in Madinah, namely His saying: "And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price..." to His saying "...what they used to do" (16:95-97). al-Shaʿbi said: it is Makkan except "And if you retaliate..." to the end of the verses (16:126-128). Qatadah said: it is Makkan except five verses. Muqatil said: it is Makkan except seven verses. Jabir ibn Zayd said: forty verses from the beginning of al-Naḥl were revealed in Makkah, and the rest in Madinah. It is narrated from ʿAli ibn Zayd who said: al-Naḥl was called "the Surah of Blessings" because of the many blessings enumerated in it. See: Zad al-Masir: 4/425-426; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/107.]]. ﷽

* *

﴿Atā﴾ means came, drew near and approached. ﴿Amru Allāh﴾ (the command of Allah). Ibn ʿArafah said: The Arabs say, "The matter has come to you" when it is still expected. That is, "The command of Allah has come," meaning its promised occurrence is imminent, so do not seek to hasten it.

﴿Amru Allāh﴾: al-Kalbi and others said: what is meant by it is the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When Allah the Exalted revealed His saying, ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ (54:1), the disbelievers said to one another, "This man claims that the Resurrection has drawn near. So refrain from some of what you have been doing until you see what will happen." When nothing came, [they said, "We see nothing."] Then the verse "Their reckoning has drawn near for people" (21:1) was revealed, so they became apprehensive. When the days lengthened, they said, "O Muhammad, we see nothing of what you threaten us with." [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) jumped up, and the people raised their heads, thinking that it had truly arrived. Then it was revealed: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾, and they were reassured. [[Al-Wahidi narrated it in *Asbab al-Nuzul* (*The Occasions of Revelation*), p. 321, without an isnad. A similar report is narrated by al-Tabari: 14/75. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/108; al-Qurtubi: 10/66.]]

Al-Istiʿjal (seeking to hasten) means seeking a thing before its appointed time.

When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his two fingers, "and it nearly overtakes me." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in *al-Musnad*: 2/50. Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*: 11/348: "Ahmad and al-Tabari narrated it, and its chain is good." The original hadith is in al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq: 11/347, and in Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan: 4/2268. The author also narrated it in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 15/98.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The sending of the Prophet (ﷺ) was one of the signs of the Hour. When Jibril (peace be upon him) passed by the inhabitants of the heavens, sent to Muhammad (ﷺ), they said, "Allahu Akbar, the Hour has come."

Others said: what is meant by "the command" here is the punishment of those who denied, and the chastisement by the sword. This is because al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky." So he hastened the punishment, and this verse was revealed. [[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 321.]] al-Nadr was killed on the day of Badr by being executed in cold blood.

﴿Subḥānahu wa taʿālā ʿammā yushrikūn﴾ (Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him). Its meaning: He is magnified above what the polytheists ascribe to Him, through His praiseworthy attributes.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 2:

﴿He sends down the angels﴾ The common reading (al-'amma) is with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the zāy, and ﴿the angels﴾ is in the accusative. Ya'qub read it with a tā' and a fatḥa on it, with a fatḥa on the zāy, and "al-malā'ikatu" (the angels) in the nominative. ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit﴾, that is, with the revelation (al-wahy). He named it "spirit" because by it hearts and truth are given life.

ʿAṭāʾ said: "with prophethood" (al-nubuwwa).

Qatada said: "with mercy" (al-raḥma).

Abu ʿUbayda said: "with the Spirit" means "together with the Spirit," and that is Jibril (Gabriel).

﴿by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants, that they warn﴾, that is, inform: ﴿that there is no god but I, so fear Me﴾.

It was also said: its meaning is, "Command them to say 'There is no god but Allah,' warning and frightening them with the Qur'an if they do not say it."

As for His saying ﴿so fear Me﴾, it means "so fear Me."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 3–7:

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth; exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ That is: He is exalted above what they associate with Him.

﴿He created man from a drop of semen, and behold, he is an open adversary﴾, quarrelsome in falsehood.

It was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, who denied the Resurrection. He brought a crumbled bone and said: "Do you claim that Allah, exalted is He, will bring this back to life after it has decayed?" As Allah, dhikruhu jalla, said: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation﴾ [Yasin: 77]. It was also revealed concerning him. [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 322; al-Qurtubi: 10/67; Zad al-Masir: 4/428.]]

The correct view is that the verse is general, and it contains a demonstration of power and an exposure of the ugliness of what they did, namely denying the blessings of Allah despite their being evident to them. [[This is what al-Tabari preferred, where he said: "By al-insan he means all people; it is expressed in the singular but has the meaning of the plural," and Ibn 'Atiyyah inclined to it in his tafsir. The mentioned occasion of revelation enters into the meaning of the verse, and the verse remains more general. See: al-Tabari: 14/78; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 8/370.]] His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the cattle He created for you; in them is warmth for you﴾, meaning the camels, cows and sheep, ﴿and benefits﴾, meaning from their wool, hair and fleece, garments and coverings with which you keep warm; ﴿and benefits﴾ through breeding, milk, riding, carrying and other things; ﴿and from them you eat﴾, meaning their meat.

﴿And for you in them is beauty﴾, adornment, ﴿when you bring them back in the evening﴾, that is, when you return them at dusk from their pastures to their resting places where they shelter, ﴿and when you send them out in the morning﴾, that is, you drive them out at dawn from their pens to their grazing grounds. He mentioned the bringing back first because benefits are taken from them after they return, and their owner is more pleased with them when they come back.

﴿And they carry your loads﴾, your burdens, ﴿to a land﴾ other than your land. 'Ikrimah said: the land is Makkah. ﴿which you could not reach except with great hardship﴾, that is, with difficulty and effort. Ash-shiqq also means half; that is, you could not reach it except with the loss of the strength of your souls and the depletion of half of them.

Abu Ja'far recited ﴿bi-shiqq﴾ with a fatha on the shin, and both are dialectal forms, like ratl and ritl.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ toward His creation, in that He made these benefits available to them.

(Qur'an 16:8) ﴿And the horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment﴾ — meaning: and He created the horses. "Horse" (khayl) is a collective noun with no singular form from its own root, like "camels" (ibil) and "women" (nisa').

﴿And the mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment﴾ — meaning: He made them an adornment for you, along with the benefits they provide.

Those who hold that eating horse meat is forbidden cite this verse, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas. He recited this verse and said: "This is for riding." This is also the view of al-Hakam, Malik, and Abu Hanifah.

A group held that horse meat is permissible, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Shurayh, 'Ata', and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq also said so. [See in detail: Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 5/2-4; Ahkam al-Qur'an by Ibn al-'Arabi 3/1144-1147; Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Harrasi al-Tabari 4/170; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 10/76-79.]

Those who permit it say: the verse is not intended to explain what is lawful and unlawful, but rather to inform the servants of God of His blessings and to alert them to the perfection of His power and wisdom. They argued with the following:

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, who said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Amr (that is, Ibn Dinar), from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the meat of donkeys on the day of Khaybar and permitted the meat of horses." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Hunting and Slaughtering, chapter on the meat of horses, 9/648, and by Muslim in Hunting and Slaughtering, chapter on eating horse meat, no. 1941, 3/1541. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/254.]

We were informed by Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Isma'il al-Tamimi, who was informed by Abu al-Qasim Hamzah ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi, who was informed by Abu Ahmad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Adi al-Hafiz, who said: al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj narrated to us, who said: 'Amr ibn Khalid narrated to us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Karim narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir: that they used to eat horse meat during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [Narrated by Abu Dawud in Foods, chapter on eating horse meat, 5/308; al-Tirmidhi in Foods, chapter on horse meat, 5/505; al-Nasa'i in Hunting and Slaughtering, chapter on permission to eat horse meat, 7/202; Ibn Majah in Slaughtering, chapter on mule meat, no. 3191, 2/1064; al-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar 2/322; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 4/235; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 3/356; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/256. The original hadith is in the Two Sahihs. See also Nasb al-Rayah 4/197 and Talkhis al-Habir 4/150.]

He (ﷺ) forbade the meat of mules and donkeys. It was narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib, from Khalid ibn al-Walid, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade eating the meat of horses, mules and donkeys. [Narrated by Abu Dawud in Foods, chapter on eating horse meat, 5/308, who said: "This is abrogated, and a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) ate horse meat: Ibn al-Zubayr, Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, Anas ibn Malik, Asma' bint Abi Bakr, and Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, may Allah be pleased with them; and Quraysh used to slaughter them during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ)." Al-Mundhiri said: the hadith is weak; see also 5/316-317. The author also weakened it, as you see. It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i in Hunting and Slaughtering, chapter on the prohibition of eating horse meat, 7/202; Ibn Majah in the same place, 2/1066; al-Daraqutni in Hunting and Slaughtering, 4/287; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad. Al-Sindi in his commentary on al-Nasa'i reported the scholars' agreement on the weakness of this hadith, and some of them said it is abrogated. See also Talkhis al-Habir 4/150-151 and Nasb al-Rayah 4/196.] Its chain is weak.

﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾ — it was said: this means what Allah has prepared in Paradise for its people and in the Fire for its people, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.

Qatadah said: it means the weevil in plants and the worm in fruits.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 9–10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ means: the explanation of the path of guidance from misguidance. It was also said: the explanation of the truth through signs and proofs. And al-qasd (the straight course) is the straight path.

﴿And among it is that which deviates﴾ means: and among the ways there is one that deviates from uprightness and is crooked. So the straight course of the way is the religion of Islam, and that which deviates from it is Judaism, Christianity, and all the other creeds of disbelief.

Jabir ibn Abdullah said: "Qasd al-sabil" is the explanation of the laws (shara'i') and the obligatory duties (fara'id).

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and Sahl ibn Abdullah said: "Qasd al-sabil" is the Sunnah, and "and among it is that which deviates" refers to the desires (ahwa') and innovations (bid'ah). Its evidence is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

﴿And had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾. Its parallel is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13].

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky; from it is drink for you﴾, which you drink, ﴿and from it [grows] trees﴾, meaning: from that water comes the drink of your trees and the life of your vegetation, ﴿in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ means: in the trees, you graze your livestock.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 15–16:**

﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it shake with you﴾. That is, [so that it would not shake with you] [[Addition from manuscript "b".]], meaning it would move and sway.

Al-mayd (sway, a state of agitation and tilting) is what this word denotes. From it comes the term *mayad* for the dizziness that afflicts a sea traveller.

Wahb said: When God created the earth, it began to sway, so the angels said: "This will not let anyone stand firm upon its back." It then became settled by the mountains, and the angels did not know what the mountains were created from.

﴿And rivers and roads﴾. That is, He placed in it rivers and various paths, ﴿so that you may be guided﴾ to what you seek, so that you do not go astray.

﴿And landmarks﴾, meaning signposts of the roads. Some of them said: Here the speech is complete, and then a new one begins: ﴿and by the star they are guided﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Kalbi said: By the landmarks He meant the mountains. The mountains serve as landmarks by day, and the stars serve as landmarks by night.

Mujahid said: By all of it He meant the stars. Some of them serve as landmarks, and others are used for guidance.

Al-Suddi said: By the star He meant the Pleiades, the Wagon (Banat Na'sh), the two Guards (al-Farqadan), and the Pole Star (al-Jadi), by which one is guided to roads and the qibla.

Qatadah said: God created the stars for three things: to be an adornment for the sky, as landmarks for the roads, and as projectiles against the devils. Whoever says other than this has presumed to speak about what he has no knowledge of.

[[Recorded by al-Bukhari in suspended form (ta'liq) in Bad' al-Khalq, chapter on the stars (6/295). It was connected by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/91–92). It was also recorded by Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abd ibn Humayd, with the following addition at its end: "Indeed, some ignorant people concerning God's command have invented fortune-telling with these stars: whoever plants by such-and-such a star, it will be thus, and whoever travels by such-and-such a star, it will be thus. By my life, there is no star that does not coincide with the birth of a tall or short person, a red or white person, a beautiful or ugly person. Knowledge of these stars, this creature, and this bird is not part of the unseen." See: Fath al-Bari (6/295), Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/397). For the ruling on astrology (tanjim) and a detailed discussion of it, see: Tafsir al-Qurtubi (11/1; 19/28–29), Fath al-Majid Sharh Kitab al-Tawhid (pp. 365–370), and Alam al-Ghayb wa al-Shahadah by Uthman Jumu'ah Dumayriyyah (pp. 128–131).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 17–22:

﴿Is He who creates like one who does not create?﴾ Meaning: Allah, the Exalted, ﴿is like one who does not create﴾, meaning the idols. ﴿Will you not then be reminded?﴾

﴿And if you were to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of your shortcomings in thanking Him for His favours, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward you, in that He has extended His favours upon you and has not cut them off from you because of your negligence and disobedience.

﴿And those they invoke besides Allah﴾ meaning: the idols. ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read "yadʿūna" (they invoke) with the letter yāʾ.

﴿They create nothing, while they are created﴾. ﴿They are dead, not alive﴾, i.e., the idols. ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾, meaning the idols. ﴿When﴾ (ayyāna), meaning when, ﴿they will be raised up﴾. The Qur'an indicates that the idols will be raised up and given life, whereupon they will disown their worshippers.

It is also said: the disbelieving idol-worshippers do not know when they will be resurrected. His Exalted saying: ﴿Your God is one God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are denying﴾, i.e., rejecting, ﴿and they are arrogant﴾, i.e., magnifying themselves.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 16, verses 23–25:**

﴿Undoubtedly﴾, truly, ﴿Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.﴾

Abu Sa'id Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmi al-Bastami related to us. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Sakhtawayh related to us. Abu al-Fadl Sufyan ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari related to us. Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Isa al-Hilali related to us, from Yahya ibn Hammad, from Shu'bah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Fudayl al-Fuqaymi, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Alqamah ibn Qays, from Abd Allah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one who has in his heart an atom's weight of arrogance will enter Paradise, and no one who has in his heart an atom's weight of faith will enter Hellfire." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man likes his clothes to be fine?" He said: "Indeed, Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter on the prohibition of arrogance and its explanation, no. (91): 1/93, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/165.]]

﴿And when it is said to them﴾, meaning: to those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they are the polytheists of Mecca who divided its mountain passes ['aqabah, plural: 'aqabat; see above, Surah al-Hijr, verse 9] whenever the pilgrims asked them, ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples."﴾ Their tales and falsehoods.

﴿So that they will bear their burdens﴾, the sins of their own selves, ﴿in full﴾. He mentioned "in full" because the afflictions that befall them in this world and the good deeds they do do not expiate anything for them, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾, without proof, so they turn them away from faith, ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾, what they carry.

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi related to us. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Tays-funi related to us. Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari related to us. Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani related to us. Ali ibn Hujr related to us. Isma'il ibn Ja'far related to us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing their rewards in any way. And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing their sins in any way." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Knowledge, chapter on whoever establishes a good or bad practice, no. (2674): 4/2060, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/232.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 16, verses 26–28:**

Allah's words: ﴿Those before them had already plotted﴾. This refers to Nimrod ibn Kan'an, who built the tower at Babil (Babylon) so that he could ascend to the heaven.

Ibn 'Abbas and Wahb said: The height of the tower in the sky was five thousand cubits (dhira', a unit of length).

Ka'b and Muqatil said: Its height was two farsakh (a unit of distance, roughly three miles). Then a wind blew and cast its top into the sea, and the rest of it collapsed upon them while they were beneath it. When the tower fell, people's tongues became confused from the terror of that day, so they spoke seventy-three languages. For this reason it was named Babil. Before that, the language of the people had been Syriac (al-Suryaniyyah).[[There is no authentic report from the Infallible (ﷺ) concerning this tower, its height, or the confusion of tongues, etc., to which one may turn. These and similar accounts are taken from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives transmitted from Jewish and Christian sources). And Allah knows best.]] This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So Allah came at their building from its foundations﴾, that is, He targeted their structure at its roots. ﴿And the roof fell down upon them from above them﴾, meaning the upper parts of the houses. ﴿And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾, from their place of safety.

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them﴾, that is, He will humiliate them with punishment, ﴿and say: "Where are My partners, about whom you used to oppose [the believers]?"﴾, that is, you used to oppose the believers concerning them. "Why do they not appear to you so that they may repel the punishment from you?"

Nafi' read the nun in ﴿tushaqqoon﴾ with a kasra (تُشَاقِّّونَ) as an idafah construction, while the others read it with a fatha (تُشَاقُّونَ).

﴿Those who were given knowledge will say﴾ [and they are the believers]: ﴿Indeed, disgrace (al-khizy) today and evil (al-su') are upon the disbelievers﴾. Al-khizy means humiliation, and al-su' means punishment. ﴿Those whom the angels take in death﴾, that is, the Angel of Death and his helpers seize their souls. Hamzah read ﴿yatawaffahum﴾ (يَتَوَفَّاهُمْ) with a ya', and likewise what follows it. ﴿While wronging themselves﴾ by disbelief. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: in the state of their disbelief. ﴿Then they will offer submission﴾, that is, they will surrender and submit, saying: ﴿"We did not used to do any evil"﴾, meaning polytheism. The angels will say to them: ﴿"Yes, indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do"﴾.

'Ikrimah said: By this he meant those disbelievers who were killed at Badr.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 29–32:**

﴿Then enter﴾, meaning: it will be said to them, "Enter ﴿the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾", those who were arrogant towards faith.

﴿And it will be said to those who feared God﴾. This was because the tribes of the Arabs used to send, during the season of the markets, someone who would come to them with news of the Prophet (ﷺ). When he came, he would ask those who sat along the roads about him. They would say: "He is a sorcerer, a kahin (soothsayer), a poet, a liar, a madman." They would add: "It would be better for you not to meet him." The questioner would say: "I would be the worst envoy if I returned to my people without entering Makkah and meeting him." So he would enter Makkah, see the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they would inform him of his truthfulness and that he was a prophet sent by God. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And it will be said to those who feared God: "What has your Lord sent down?" They will say: "Good."﴾ That is, He sent down good.

Then He began, saying: ﴿For those who did good in this world there is a good reward﴾, as an honour from God.

Ibn Abbas said: it is the multiplying of the reward up to ten-fold.

al-Dahhak said: it is victory and conquest.

Mujahid said: it is goodly provision.

﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better﴾, that is, the Home of the state of the Hereafter, ﴿and excellent is the home of the God-fearing﴾. al-Hasan said: it is this world, because the people of piety gather provision in it for the Hereafter. Most of the exegetes said: it is Paradise. Then He explained it, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow; for them therein is whatever they wish. Thus does God reward the God-fearing﴾. ﴿Those whom the angels take in a state of purity﴾, believing and pure from polytheism.

Mujahid said: their deeds and words are pure.

It was also said: its meaning is that their death occurs in a good and easy manner.

﴿They will say﴾, meaning: the angels will say to them, ﴿"Peace be upon you."﴾ It was also said: they convey to them the peace of God. ﴿"Enter Paradise because of what you used to do."﴾

﴿And it will be said to those who feared God﴾. This was because the tribes of the Arabs used to send, during the season of the markets, someone who would come to them with news of the Prophet (ﷺ). When he came, he would ask those who sat along the roads about him. They would say: "He is a sorcerer, a kahin (soothsayer), a poet, a liar, a madman." They would add: "It would be better for you not to meet him." The questioner would say: "I would be the worst envoy if I returned to my people without entering Makkah and meeting him." So he would enter Makkah, see the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they would inform him of his truthfulness and that he was a prophet sent by God. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And it will be said to those who feared God: "What has your Lord sent down?" They will say: "Good."﴾ That is, He sent down good.

Then He began, saying: ﴿For those who did good in this world there is a good reward﴾, as an honour from God.

Ibn Abbas said: it is the multiplying of the reward up to ten-fold.

al-Dahhak said: it is victory and conquest.

Mujahid said: it is goodly provision.

﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better﴾, that is, the Home of the state of the Hereafter, ﴿and excellent is the home of the God-fearing﴾. al-Hasan said: it is this world, because the people of piety gather provision in it for the Hereafter. Most of the exegetes said: it is Paradise. Then He explained it, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow; for them therein is whatever they wish. Thus does God reward the God-fearing﴾. ﴿Those whom the angels take in a state of purity﴾, believing and pure from polytheism.

Mujahid said: their deeds and words are pure.

It was also said: its meaning is that their death occurs in a good and easy manner.

﴿They will say﴾, meaning: the angels will say to them, ﴿"Peace be upon you."﴾ It was also said: they convey to them the peace of God. ﴿"Enter Paradise because of what you used to do."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 33–36:

His the Mighty and Majestic's saying: ﴿Do they await only that the angels should come to them﴾ to seize their souls, ﴿or that the command of your Lord should come﴾ meaning: the Day of Resurrection; and it has been said: the punishment.

﴿Thus did those before them act﴾, that is, they disbelieved, ﴿and Allah did not wrong them﴾ by punishing them, ﴿but they were wronging themselves.﴾ ﴿So the evil consequences of what they had done struck them﴾: the penalties of their disbelief and their wicked deeds. ﴿And there encompassed them﴾ [came down upon them] [[Omitted from "b".]] ﴿what they used to mock at.﴾

﴿And those who associated others with Allah said: "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped other than Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything without His permission."﴾ Meaning: the baheera, the saaiba, the waseela and the haam. "Had Allah been pleased with them, He would have changed that and guided us to other than them." ﴿Thus did those before them act. Then is upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ That is: guidance is not up to them; rather, their duty is only to convey.

﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾ That is, just as We sent among you, ﴿saying: "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ and the taghut is everything worshipped besides Allah. ﴿So among them were those whom Allah guided﴾ that is, Allah guided him to His religion, ﴿and among them were those upon whom error was deserved.﴾

That is: it became binding by the prior decree, until he died upon his disbelief. ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ That is: the final outcome of their affair, which was the ruin of their dwellings through punishment and destruction.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 37–40:

﴿If you are eager for their guidance, [O Muhammad], indeed Allah does not guide those He leads astray.﴾ Ahl al-Kufah (the people of Kufa) read "yahdi" with a fatha on the yā' and a kasra on the dāl, meaning: Allah does not guide the one whom He has led astray. It was also said: its meaning is that the one whom Allah has led astray does not become guided.

The others read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatha on the dāl, meaning: whomever Allah leads astray, there is no guide for him, as He said: "And whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him" [Al-A'raf: 186].

﴿And they will have no helpers﴾, meaning: no one who will prevent them from the punishment. His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die.﴾ They were deniers of the Resurrection. Allah, exalted is He, responded to them: ﴿Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, true, but most of the people do not know.﴾

﴿So that He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾, meaning: so that He may make the truth manifest to them regarding what they differ about. ﴿And so that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.﴾

﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ Allah, exalted is He, says: when We intend to resurrect the dead, there is no toil upon Us in bringing them back to life, nor in anything else that comes into being. We only say to it, "Be," and it is.

Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah says: My servant has denied Me, and he had no right to do so; and My servant has reviled Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: He will not bring us back as He originated us. And as for his reviling Me, it is his saying: Allah has taken a son. And I am the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad); I did not beget, nor was I begotten, and there is none equal to Me."

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, Surat al-Baqarah, chapter "And they said: Allah has taken a son, glorified is He," 8/168.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 41–43:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah after they had been wronged﴾, meaning they were tortured and harmed for the sake of Allah.

It was revealed concerning Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Abis, Jabr, and Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl, whom the polytheists of Makkah seized and tortured [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 322; Zad al-Masir: 4/448, where it reads "Ayash" instead of "Abis," and I have not found a biography of "Ayash." Compare al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 8/421.]].

Qatadah said: They are the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. The people of Makkah wronged them and expelled them from their homes, until a group of them joined the Abyssinians. Then Allah settled them in Madinah afterwards, made it a land of emigration (dar hijrah) for them, and appointed for them helpers from among the believers [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/131; al-Tabari: 14/107.]].

﴿We will surely settle them in this world in a good place﴾, which is that He housed them in Madinah.

It is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab that whenever he gave a man among the emigrants (al-Muhajirin) a grant, he would say: "Take it; may Allah bless it for you. This is what Allah promised you in this world, and what He has stored up for you in the Hereafter is better." Then he recited this verse [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/493; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 8/422.]].

It was also said: its meaning is that We will treat them well in this world.

It was also said: the "good" in this world is success (tawfiq) and guidance.

﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾. His saying, ﴿if only they knew﴾, refers to the polytheists, because the believers already knew it.

﴿Those who were patient﴾ for the sake of Allah in what befell them, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

﴿We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed⁠﴾. It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah, when they denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and said: "Allah is greater than that His messenger should be a human being. Why did He not send an angel to us?" [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 323; al-Tabari: 14/109; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/132–133.]] ﴿So ask the people of the reminder﴾, meaning the believers among the People of the Book, ﴿if you do not know﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 44–47:

﴿with the clear proofs and the scriptures﴾. The scholars differed concerning what governs the preposition *bi* (with) in His words ﴿with the clear proofs﴾. It was said: it refers back to His words ﴿And We did not send﴾, and *illa* is used in the sense of *ghayr* (other than). Its meaning is: "And We did not send before you [any] other than men to whom We revealed, with the clear proofs and the scriptures, and We did not send angels."

It was also said: its interpretation is, "And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed [We sent them] with the clear proofs and the scriptures." [[The words "[We sent them]" are missing from manuscript "b".]]

﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, so that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾. He meant by "the Reminder" the revelation, and the Prophet ﷺ was the one who explained the revelation, and the explanation of the Book is sought from the Sunnah (the prophetic example and practice). ﴿And perhaps they will reflect﴾.

﴿Do those who devised evil deeds feel secure﴾, that is, those who did ﴿the evil deeds﴾ before, meaning Nimrod ibn Kan'an and others among the disbelievers, ﴿that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive?﴾ ﴿Or He will seize them﴾ with punishment, ﴿in their going back and forth﴾, that is, their movements in journeys. Ibn Abbas said: "in their differing." Ibn Jurayj said: "in their coming and going." ﴿So they cannot escape﴾, that is, they cannot outrun Allah.

﴿Or He will seize them by gradual wasting away﴾. The *takhawwuf* is the diminishing, meaning that He reduces from their borders and their surroundings a little at a time until all of them perish. It is said: "Time (al-dahr) gradually wasted him (takhawwafahu al-dahr) and took from him (takhawwanahu)," when it diminishes him, takes his wealth, and his household.

It is said: this is the dialect of the Banu Hudhayl.

Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: it means "from fear," that is, He punishes one group so that the others fear that what befell them will befall them too.

﴿Indeed your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾, in that He did not hasten the punishment.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 48–49:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created?﴾ Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with the "ta'" (tu-), in the form of direct address (khitab), and likewise in Surat al-Ankabut; the others read it with the "ya'" (yu-), as a report about those who schemed evil deeds (alladhina makarus-sayyi'at). ﴿...to what things Allah has created of a thing (shay') possessing a body, standing, having a shadow, that ﴾ ﴿yatafayya'u﴾ (casts about) — Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read it with the "ta'" (tatafayya'u), and the others with the "ya'" (yatafayya'u).

﴿Its shadows﴾: that is, they incline and turn from side to side. In the early part of the day they are in one state, then they contract, then in the late part of the day they return to another state, prostrating (sujjadan) to Allah. So their inclining and turning is their prostration to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The shadow in the evening is called fay', because it "faa'a," that is, it returned from the west to the east; so fay' means return. And sujud means inclination. It is said: "The palm tree prostrated (sajadat) when it leaned."

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah﴾. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: As for the right (al-yamin), it is the early part of the day, and the left (al-shimal) is the late part of the day; the shadows prostrate to Allah.

Al-Kalbi said: Before the sun rises, the shadow is on your right and your left, in front of you and behind you; likewise when it sets. When the sun rises, it is in front of you; when it has risen high, it is on your right; then after that it is behind you; and when it is before the sun sets, it is on your left. This is its casting about (tafayyu'uhu) and its turning (taqallubuhu), and this is its prostration.

Mujahid said: When the sun passes its zenith (zalat), everything prostrates to Allah.

It has also been said: what is meant by the shadows is the prostration of the bodies (ashkhas).

If it is asked: why did He use the singular for "right" and the plural for "left"?

It is said: it is among the practices of the Arabs, when two signs are combined, to suffice with one, as in His saying, ﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7], and His saying: "He brings them out of darkness into light" [al-Baqarah: 257].

It has also been said: "the right" (al-yamin) refers back to "what Allah has created," and the word "ma" is singular, while "the left" (al-shama'il) refers back to the meaning.

﴿And they are humbled (dakhirun)﴾: abased (saghirun).

﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: He reported it with the neuter (ma) because the non-rational outnumber the rational in number, and the judgment follows the majority, as the masculine is given precedence over the feminine. ﴿Of living creature (min dabbah)﴾: He meant every animal that crawls (yadibb). It is said: sujud means obedience, and all things are obedient to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, both animate and inanimate, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "We come willingly (ta'i'in)"﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

It has also been said: the prostration of things is their submission and their being subjected to, and made to serve, that for which they were intended and subjugated.

It has also been said: the prostration of inanimate things and what has no intellect is the appearance of the trace of craftsmanship in them, in the sense that it calls the heedless to prostrate upon reflection and contemplation of it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

﴿And the angels (al-mala'ikah)﴾: He singled out the angels for mention, although they are among what is in the heavens and the earth, as an honour and an elevation of their station.

It has also been said: because they are excluded from those described as crawling, since they have wings with which they fly.

It has also been said: He meant: "And to Allah prostrates what is in the heavens of the angels and what is on the earth of living creatures, and the angels prostrate."

﴿And they are not arrogant (la yastakbirun)﴾.

﴿And they are not arrogant (la yastakbirun)﴾.

﴿They fear their Lord above them﴾, like His saying: "He is the Subduer over His servants" [al-An'am: 18].

﴿And they do what they are commanded﴾

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Muhammad ibn Sam'an related to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sha'rani related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli related to us: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Absi related to us: Isra'il related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Muwarriq, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I see what you do not see, and I hear what you do not hear. The sky has creaked, and it has the right to creak. There is not a place in it the size of four fingers without an angel in it glorifying Allah. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on your beds, and you would go out to the high ground, crying out to Allah." Abu Dharr said: "Would that I were a tree that is cut down."

Abu Isa [al-Tirmidhi] narrated it from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, from Isra'il, and he said: "except that there is an angel placing his forehead in prostration to Allah."

[Cited in al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of weeping out of fear of Allah: 6/601, where he said, "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Also in Ibn Majah, Kitab al-Zuhd, chapter on sorrow and weeping: 2/1402. Al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 2/510. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 5/173. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/369-370.]

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And Allah said: Do not take two gods; He is only one God, so fear Me alone﴾ ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is the religion﴾, meaning obedience and sincerity, ﴿enduring﴾ meaning lasting and constant.

Its meaning: There is no one to whom obedience is owed and who is obeyed except that this ends for him by cessation or destruction, other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for obedience to Him endures and does not end.

﴿Then is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ meaning: do you fear, as a rhetorical question in the form of denunciation.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 53–58:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾, meaning: whatever blessing you have, it is from Allah. ﴿Then when harm touches you, such as famine and sickness, to Him you cry out﴾, meaning you wail and shout in supplication and appeal for help.

﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord﴾.

﴿So that they may deny﴾, meaning so that they may reject [the truth]. [This lam is called the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning the final outcome of their affair is their disbelief.] ﴿what We have given them﴾, meaning what We have bestowed upon them of favours, the removal of hardship and affliction. ﴿So enjoy yourselves﴾, meaning live in this world for the term We have set for you. ﴿But you will soon know﴾ the outcome of your affair. This is a warning to them.

﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share﴾ of what they possess, meaning to the idols, ﴿of what We have provided for them﴾ of wealth. This is what they set aside for the idols from their crops and livestock, saying: "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "this is for our partners."

Then he turned from the report to direct address, saying: ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿about what you used to fabricate﴾ in the world.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters﴾ — and they are Khuza'ah and Kinanah, who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah, may He be exalted — ﴿Glory be to Him! And for themselves is what they desire﴾, meaning they assign to themselves the sons whom they desire. Here "ma" is in the accusative position, and it is also permissible that it be in the nominative position as a subject, in which case "ma" is in the nominative position.

﴿And when one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes dark﴾, changed from grief and aversion, ﴿and he is filled with suppressed rage﴾, meaning he is full of sorrow and anger, so he suppresses it (yakzimuhu), that is, he holds it back and does not show it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 53–58:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 59–60:

﴿He hides himself from the people because of the evil of that which he has been given tidings of﴾, i.e., he conceals himself, out of grief and shame. ﴿Then he reflects: "Shall he keep it despite disgrace, or bury it in the dust?"﴾ He mentioned the pronominal reference (al-kinaya, the pronoun) as a response to "má" (what). ﴿Despite disgrace﴾, i.e., humiliation. ﴿Or bury it in the dust﴾ 200/b, i.e., conceal it from him, so that he buries it alive (ya'idu, wa'd).

The reason for this: Mudar, Khuza'a and Tamim used to bury their daughters alive, out of fear of poverty for themselves and the desire of unequal suitors for them. When a man among the Arabs had a daughter born to him and wished to spare her, he would dress her in a garment of wool or hair and leave her to tend his camels and sheep in the desert. But when he wished to kill her, he would leave her until she reached the age of six (sudasiyya), then he would say to her mother: "Adorn her, so that I may take her to her in-laws." He would have dug a well for her in the desert. When he brought her to the well, he would say to her: "Look at this well," and then push her from behind into it, and then heap earth over her head until the well is level with the ground. This is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿Shall he keep it despite disgrace, or bury it in the dust?﴾

Sa'sa'a, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, whenever he sensed something of this, would send camels to the father of the girl, to revive her by means of that. Al-Farazdaq boasted of this, saying [[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/117.]]:

"My uncle, who prevented the girls from being buried,
So he revived the buried one, and she was not buried."

﴿Surely evil is what they judge﴾: evil is what they decide, attributing daughters to Allah and sons to themselves. Its parallel is: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [al-Najm: 22]. It was also said: evil is their judgement, the burying of daughters.

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., for these who attribute daughters to Allah and sons to themselves, ﴿is the evil similitude﴾: the evil attribute of needing offspring, hatred of females, and killing them for fear of poverty. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest similitude﴾: the highest attribute, which is tawhid (affirming the oneness of Allah) and that there is no god but Him.

It was also said: it is all the attributes of majesty and perfection, such as knowledge, power, permanence, and other attributes.

Ibn Abbas said: "The evil similitude" is the Fire, and "the highest similitude" is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 16, verses 63–66:**

﴿By Allah, We certainly sent [messengers] to communities before you﴾, just as We sent [messengers] to this community, ﴿and Satan made their deeds appear fair to them﴾, the wicked deeds, ﴿so he is their guardian﴾, their helper, ﴿today﴾, and their companion. He called him their guardian (walī) because of their obedience to him. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿We did not send down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that over which they differ﴾, concerning the religion and the rulings, ﴿and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾. That is: We did not send down the Book to you except as a clarification, a guidance, and a mercy. So "guidance and mercy" are coordinated (ʿaṭf, grammatical conjunction) with his saying "that you may make clear" (litubayyina).

﴿And Allah sent down from the sky water﴾, meaning rain, ﴿and gave life thereby to the earth﴾ with vegetation, ﴿after its death﴾, after its dryness. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾, meaning the hearing of the hearts, not the hearing of the ears.

﴿And indeed, for you in livestock is a lesson﴾, an admonition. ﴿We give you drink﴾ with a fatḥah on the nūn here and in [Surah] al-Mu'minun. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Bakr, and Yaʿqūb read it with a ḍammah on the nūn, while the rest read it with a ḍammah. Both are dialectal forms (lughatān).

﴿From what is in their bellies﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: he returned the pronoun (al-kināya, the pronominal reference) to the cattle (naʿam), and naʿam and anʿām are the same.

The word naʿam is masculine. Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: naʿam may be treated as masculine or feminine. Whoever treats it as feminine does so in view of the meaning of plurality, and whoever treats it as masculine does so in view of the grammatical form of the word.

Al-Kisāʾī said: he returned the pronoun to what is meant, i.e., in the bellies of what we have mentioned.

Al-Muʾarrij said: the pronominal reference is returned to a part and a portion, as if he said: "We give you drink from what is in their bellies, the milk," since not all of them have milk. The word "milk" (labanun) is implied within the sentence.

﴿From between excrement﴾, which is the digested contents of the stomach, and when it leaves the stomach it is no longer called farth (excrement), ﴿and blood﴾, ﴿pure milk﴾, free from the blood and the excrement; it has neither the color of blood nor the smell of excrement.

﴿Palatable to the drinkers﴾, pleasant, flowing smoothly down the throat.

It is said: no one has ever choked on milk.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: when the animal eats fodder and it settles in its rumen and is ground down, its lowest part becomes excrement, its middle part becomes milk, and its uppermost part becomes blood. The liver is set over them, dividing them by the decree of Allah the Exalted. So the blood flows in the veins, the milk goes to the udder, and the excrement remains as it is. [See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/124–125; Zad al-Masir: 4/464.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 68–69:

﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee﴾ i.e., He inspired it and cast into its selves, so it understood it. And al-nahl (the bee): the wasps of honey, its singular being nahlah.

﴿That take for yourselves houses in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they build﴾ — yabnun (they build). It has been the custom that its people build places for it, so it takes refuge in them. Ibn Zayd said: they are the vineyards.

﴿Then eat from all the fruits﴾ [201] Does not the meaning of "all" (kull) denote generality? It is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and she has been given of everything﴾ [al-Naml: 23].

﴿Then follow the ways of your Lord, made easy﴾ It was said: dhulul is an adjective of the paths, meaning: they are made easy for the bee, with easy passageways. 

Mujahid said: no place is difficult for it to traverse that it has taken.

Others said: dhulul is an adjective of the bees, i.e., obedient and submissive by subjugation. It is said that its keepers move it from place to place, and it has a leader (ya'sub); when he stops, it stops, and when he moves, it moves.

﴿There comes out from their bellies a drink﴾ meaning: honey, ﴿varying in its colours﴾: white, red and yellow.

﴿In it is healing for mankind﴾ i.e., in the honey. Mujahid said: i.e., in the Qur'an; but the first is more preferable.

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad related to us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "My brother's stomach has loosened." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give him honey to drink." He gave him to drink, then came back and said: "I gave him to drink, but it only increased the loosening." The Prophet (ﷺ) said that to him three times. Then he came the fourth time and said: "Give him honey to drink." He said: "I have given him to drink, but it has only increased the loosening." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's belly has lied." So he gave him to drink, and he was cured. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tibb, chapter on treatment with honey, and the saying of Allah, "In it is healing for mankind": 10/139, and Muslim in al-Salam, chapter on treating with giving honey to drink, no. (2217): 4/1736-1737, the wording is his; and the author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/147.]]

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: Honey is a healing from every disease, and the Qur'an is a healing for what is in the breasts. [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/144.]]

It is also related from him that he said: "Hold fast to the two healings: the Qur'an and honey." [[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh, as a halted report (mawquf) upon Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him; and Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated it as a raised report (marfu') from the narration of Ibn Mas'ud. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/144.]]

﴿Surely in that is a sign for a people who reflect﴾ — so that they may take heed.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 70:

﴿And Allah created you, then He causes you to die﴾ as children, or youths, or elderly men. ﴿And among you is one who is returned to the most abject age﴾ the most wretched of it. Muqatil said: it means senility.

Qatada said: the most abject age is ninety years.

It was narrated from Ali that he said: the most abject age is seventy-five years. It was also said: eighty years.

﴿So that he knows nothing after having known﴾ so that he no longer understands anything after his earlier understanding. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾.

(2706): 4/2080.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 71–72:

﴿Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision.﴾ He extended it for one and restricted it for another, and He made it little and made it much.

﴿So those who are favoured do not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess,﴾ namely the slaves, ﴿so that they are equal with them in it.﴾ That is, so that they and their slaves would be equal in that. Allah the Exalted says: They are not content that they and their captives be equal in what Allah has provided them, yet they have made My slaves partners with Me in My dominion and My authority. This binds the proof upon the polytheists.

Qatadah said: This is an example that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has set forth. Is there any one of you whose slave shares with him his wife, his bedding, and his property? Then do you equate with Allah His creation and His servants?

﴿Then do they deny the blessing of Allah?﴾ by associating partners with Him. Abu Bakr recited it with the ta' (تَجْحَدُونَ, "you deny"), in view of His saying, "Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision." The others recited it with the ya' (يَجْحَدُونَ, "they deny"), in view of His saying, "so that they are equal in it."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from yourselves⦆ means women; He created from Adam his wife Hawwa' (Eve). It was also said: "from yourselves" means from your own kind, spouses.

﴿And made for you from your spouses children and grandchildren (ḥafadah)﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and al-Nakha'i said: the ḥafadah are a man's sons-in-law (akhtan), the husbands of his daughters.

It is also related from Ibn Mas'ud that they are the in-laws (aṣhar), so the meaning of the verse according to this view is: "And He made for you from your spouses sons and daughters, whom you marry off, so that through them come relatives by marriage and in-laws."

ʿIkrimah, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak said: they are the servants (khadam).

Mujahid said: they are the helpers; whoever helps you has served you (ḥafadak).

ʿAta' said: they are the grandchildren of a man, who help him and serve him.

Qatadah said: they are a service, who serve you and attend to you, from your children.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: "the sons" are the young ones, and "the ḥafadah" are the grown children who help him in his work.

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbas that they are the grandchildren.

Al-ʿAwfi related from him that they are the children of a man's wife who are not his own.

[Having cited the reports in the interpretation of this verse, al-Tabari (may Allah have mercy on him) said (14/146–147): "The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is to say that Allah the Exalted informed His servants, reminding them of His blessings upon them in what He has made for them of spouses and sons, saying: 'And Allah has made for you spouses from yourselves, and made for you from your spouses sons and grandchildren.' So He informed them that He made for them from their spouses sons and grandchildren. The ḥafadah in the speech of the Arabs are the plural of ḥāfid, and the ḥāfid in their speech is one who is light in service and work; ḥafd means lightness in work. If the meaning of ḥafadah is what we have mentioned, that they are those who hasten in serving the man and are light in it, and Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed us that among the blessings He bestowed upon us is that He made for us ḥafadah who serve us, and our children and spouses who are fit for service, from us and from others, and our in-laws who are the husbands of our daughters, from our spouses, and our servants from our captives, if they serve us, then they deserve the name ḥafadah. Allah the Exalted did not indicate, by the outward meaning of His revelation, nor through the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, nor by any rational proof, that He meant one type of ḥafadah to the exclusion of another type, while He had bestowed all of them upon us. So it is not for us to restrict it to a particular kind of ḥafadah rather than a general one, except what the community has agreed is not included. Since this is so, then each of the views we have mentioned from those we cited has a valid aspect and a line of interpretation. Yet the view closest to correctness is what we have chosen, for the evidence we have shown."]

﴿And provided you with good things﴾, from the blessings and the lawful things. ﴿Then in falsehood (al-bāṭil)﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿do they believe, and in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ That is, in tawhid and Islam.

It was also said: "al-bāṭil" is Satan, who commanded them to forbid the baḥīrah and the sā'ibah (kinds of animals they forbade), and "in the blessing of Allah" means in what Allah made lawful for them; "they disbelieve" means they deny His making it lawful.

If the meaning of ḥafadah is what we have mentioned, that they are those who hasten in serving the man and are light in it, and Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed us that among the blessings He bestowed upon us is that He made for us ḥafadah who serve us, and our children and spouses who are fit for service, from us and from others, and our in-laws who are the husbands of our daughters, from our spouses, and our servants from our captives, if they serve us, then they deserve the name ḥafadah. Allah the Exalted did not indicate, by the outward meaning of His revelation, nor through the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, nor by any rational proof, that He meant one type of ḥafadah to the exclusion of another type, while He had bestowed all of them upon us. So it is not for us to restrict it to a particular kind of ḥafadah rather than a general one, except what the community has agreed is not included. Since this is so, then each of the views we have mentioned from those we cited has a valid aspect and a line of interpretation. Yet the view closest to correctness is what we have chosen, for the evidence we have shown."]

﴿And provided you with good things﴾, from the blessings and the lawful things. ﴿Then in falsehood (al-bāṭil)﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿do they believe, and in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ That is, in tawhid and Islam.

It was also said: "al-bāṭil" is Satan, who commanded them to forbid the baḥīrah and the sā'ibah (kinds of animals they forbade), and "in the blessing of Allah" means in what Allah made lawful for them; "they disbelieve" means they deny His making it lawful.

﴿And they worship, besides God, that which owns no provision for them from the heavens﴾, meaning the rain, ﴿and the earth﴾, meaning the plants, ﴿nothing﴾. Al-Akhfash (Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash) said: it is a *badal* (a substitute, or apposition, replacing the noun before it) for "provision," meaning that they own no part of the matter of provision, neither little nor much.

Al-Farra' said: "shay'an" (nothing) is in the accusative because the verb "yarzuq" (provides) governs it; that is, it provides nothing. ﴿And they are not able﴾, meaning they have no power over anything. This describes the inability of the idols to bring benefit or ward off harm.

﴿So do not strike similitudes for God﴾, meaning do not liken Him to His creation, and do not make a partner for Him, for He is One, with no like. ﴿Indeed, God knows, and you do not know﴾, meaning that He knows the error of the similitudes you strike.

﴿God has struck a parable: a slave owned, who has power over nothing, and one whom We have provided with good provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise be to God. But most of them do not know.﴾ (16:75) ﴿God has struck a parable of two men: one of them is mute, having power over nothing, and he is a burden on his master, wherever he directs him he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice while he is upon a straight path?﴾ (16:76)

Then He struck a parable [for the disbelievers and the believers]¹ and said, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿God has struck a parable: a slave owned, who has power over nothing﴾. This is the parable of the disbeliever, whom God gave wealth, but he did not send forward any good from it. ﴿And one whom We have provided with good provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly﴾. This is the parable of the believer, whom God gave wealth, and he acted with it in obedience to God, and spent it seeking God's good pleasure, secretly and openly, so God rewarded him with Paradise for it.² 

﴿Are they equal?﴾ He did not say "are they two equal" because of the word "man" (min), which is a noun that can be used for the singular, the dual and the plural. Likewise His saying "they are not able" is in the plural, for the sake of the meaning of "what" (ma).

Its meaning: Is this poor, stingy man equal to the rich, generous man? Likewise the disbelieving sinner is not equal to the believing obedient one. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ata' concerning His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿a slave owned﴾ refers to Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, ﴿and one whom We have provided with good provision from Us﴾ refers to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him.³ Then He said:

﴿Praise be to God. But most of them do not know.﴾ He means: the matter is not as you say. The idols have no favour or kindness with them for which they should be praised. Rather, complete praise belongs to God, mighty and majestic, for He is the Giver of blessings, the Creator and the Provider. But most of the disbelievers do not know. Then He struck a parable for the idols, saying: ﴿God has struck a parable of two men: one of them is mute, having power over nothing, and he is a burden on his master﴾. *Kall* (a burden) means weight and encumbrance. ﴿On his master﴾ means on his paternal cousin and the people of his guardianship. ﴿Wherever he directs him﴾ means sends him. ﴿He brings no good﴾, because he does not understand what is said to him, nor is he understood by others. This is the parable of the idols: they do not hear, do not speak, and do not reason. ﴿And he is a burden on his master﴾, meaning his worshipper, who needs him to carry him, place him, and serve him.

﴿Is he equal to one who commands justice﴾, meaning God, who is Mighty, Speaking, commands monotheism. ﴿While he is upon a straight path﴾ [al-Kalbi said: meaning He guides you to a straight path.

It was also said: it refers to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who commands justice while he is upon a straight path.⁴

It was also said: both parables are for the believer and the disbeliever, narrated by Atiyyah from Ibn Abbas.

Ata' said: the mute man is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and the one who commands justice is Hamzah, Uthman ibn Affan, and Uthman ibn Maz'un.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Hashim ibn Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Rabi'ah al-Qurashi, who had little good in him and was hostile to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

It was also said: it was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Affan and his freed slave. Uthman used to spend on him, and his freed slave used to dislike Islam.]⁵

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 77–78:

﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and the matter of the Hour is but as the blink of an eye, or it is nearer.﴾ Meaning: in the nearness of its occurrence. ﴿But as the blink of an eye﴾ when He says to it, "Be," and it is. ﴿Or it is nearer﴾ rather, it is nearer. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ It was revealed concerning the disbelievers who were hastening the Resurrection in mockery.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, not knowing anything﴾. Al-Kisa'i read "buṭūni immahātikum" with a kasrah on the hamzah, and Hamzah read it with a kasrah on the mim and the hamzah, while the rest read it with a ḍammah on the hamzah and a fatḥah on the mim. ﴿Not knowing anything﴾ the statement is complete. Then he began, saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿And He made for you hearing and sight and hearts﴾, because Allah, Exalted is He, made these faculties for them before they came out from the wombs of their mothers, and He only granted them knowledge after they came out. ﴿That you may be grateful﴾ for the favour of Allah.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 77–78:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verse 84–88:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And on the Day We raise up from every nation a witness﴾, meaning a messenger. ﴿Then no permission will be given to those who disbelieved﴾ to make excuses, and it was said: to speak at all. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾, meaning they will not be asked to seek their Lord's pleasure (istiʿtab, to seek to be reconciled or pleased). That is, they will not be obligated to satisfy their Lord, because the Hereafter is not an abode of obligation, and they will not be returned to the world so that they might repent. The true meaning of istiʿtab is: engaging in the seeking of pleasure, and this avenue is closed to the disbelievers in the Hereafter.

﴿And when those who did wrong﴾, meaning those who disbelieved, ﴿see the punishment﴾, meaning Hell, ﴿it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ ﴿And when those who associated partners [with Allah]﴾ see on the Day of Resurrection ﴿their partners﴾, their idols, ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You"﴾ as lords, and worship them. ﴿But they will throw back at them the saying﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿"Indeed, you are liars"﴾, that is, they will say to them: you are lying in calling us gods, since we did not invite you to worship us.

﴿And they will offer submission to Allah that Day﴾, meaning the polytheists; they submit and yield to His judgment concerning them, and their gods did not avail them anything, ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, namely the claim that they would intercede for them.

﴿Those who disbelieved and barred [others] from the way of Allah﴾, who prevented people from the path of truth, ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment.﴾ ʿAbdullah [ibn Masʿud] said: scorpions having fangs like tall palm trees.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: serpents like Bukht camels [[Bukht: the Khurasani camels, which are long-necked camels; their singular is bukhti.]] and scorpions like mules; one sting from one of them causes its victim to feel its pain for forty autumns.

Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil said: this refers to five rivers of molten brass, like fire, flowing from beneath the Throne, by which they are tormented: three on the measure of the night and two on the measure of the day.

It was also said: they will pass from the heat of the Fire to the cold of the Zamharir, and from the severe cold of the Zamharir they will hasten back to the Fire, seeking refuge in it.

It was also said: the punishment will be doubled for them. [[See these opinions in: al-Durr al-Manthur 5/157-158; Zad al-Masir 4/482. al-Tabari (14/160-161) adopted the first opinion. See also: Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/582.]]

﴿Because they used to cause corruption﴾ in the world through disbelief and by barring people from faith.

﴿And when those who did wrong﴾, meaning those who disbelieved, ﴿see the punishment﴾, meaning Hell, ﴿it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ ﴿And when those who associated partners [with Allah]﴾ see on the Day of Resurrection ﴿their partners﴾, their idols, ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You"﴾ as lords, and worship them. ﴿But they will throw back at them the saying﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿"Indeed, you are liars"﴾, that is, they will say to them: you are lying in calling us gods, since we did not invite you to worship us.

﴿And they will offer submission to Allah that Day﴾, meaning the polytheists; they submit and yield to His judgment concerning them, and their gods did not avail them anything, ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, namely the claim that they would intercede for them.

﴿Those who disbelieved and barred [others] from the way of Allah﴾, who prevented people from the path of truth, ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment.﴾ ʿAbdullah [ibn Masʿud] said: scorpions having fangs like tall palm trees.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: serpents like Bukht camels [[Bukht: the Khurasani camels, which are long-necked camels; their singular is bukhti.]] and scorpions like mules; one sting from one of them causes its victim to feel its pain for forty autumns.

Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil said: this refers to five rivers of molten brass, like fire, flowing from beneath the Throne, by which they are tormented: three on the measure of the night and two on the measure of the day.

It was also said: they will pass from the heat of the Fire to the cold of the Zamharir, and from the severe cold of the Zamharir they will hasten back to the Fire, seeking refuge in it.

It was also said: the punishment will be doubled for them. [[See these opinions in: al-Durr al-Manthur 5/157-158; Zad al-Masir 4/482. al-Tabari (14/160-161) adopted the first opinion. See also: Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/582.]]

﴿Because they used to cause corruption﴾ in the world through disbelief and by barring people from faith.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 89–90:

﴿On the Day when We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves﴾: meaning, their own prophet, from among themselves, because prophets were sent to nations from among them.

﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these﴾, those to whom you were sent.

﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation﴾, a clarification, ﴿of everything﴾ that is needed from commands and prohibitions, lawful and unlawful, limits and rulings, ﴿and as guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and as mercy and good tidings﴾, glad tidings ﴿to the Muslims﴾. His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾, meaning equity, ﴿and excellence (al-Ihsan)﴾ toward people.

It is related from Ibn Abbas: "Justice (al-Adl)" is tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), and "excellence (al-Ihsan)" is performing the obligatory duties.

It is also related from him: "Excellence" is sincerity in tawhid. This is the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Excellence is that you worship God as if you see Him" [[A portion of the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, concerning the question of Gabriel, peace be upon him, about Islam, iman, and ihsan, narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Iman, chapter "The question of Gabriel to the Prophet about iman, Islam and ihsan," 1/114, and by Muslim in the Book of Iman, chapter "Explanation of iman, Islam and ihsan," no. (8), 1/36–37, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/8–9.]].

Muqatil said: "Justice" is tawhid, and "excellence" is pardoning people.

﴿And giving to kinsfolk﴾ is maintaining the ties of kinship.

﴿And He forbids indecency﴾ [202/a], meaning what is ugly of speech and deed. Ibn Abbas said: it is fornication. ﴿And wrongdoing﴾: what is not recognized in the law or the Sunnah. ﴿And oppression﴾: arrogance and injustice.

Ibn Uyaynah said: Justice is the equality of the inward and the outward. "Excellence" is that one's inner state is better than his outward appearance, and "indecency and wrongdoing" are that one's outward appearance is better than his inner state.

﴿He admonishes you, that perhaps you may take heed﴾: that you may be admonished.

Ibn Mas'ud said: the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an is this verse [[See: Al-Durr al-Manthur, 5/160, which contains a number of reports on this.]].

Ayyub related from Ikrimah: The Prophet (ﷺ) recited to al-Walid: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said to him: "O nephew, repeat it," so he repeated it to him. Then [al-Walid] said: "By God, it has a sweetness, and upon it there is a radiance, its upper part bears fruit and its lower part is abundant, and it is not the speech of a human being" [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham, 1/270.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 16, verses 91–92:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have made it﴾. Here "the covenant" (al-'ahd) means the oath (al-yamin).

Al-Sha'bi said: "The covenant is an oath, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath." ﴿And do not break your oaths after their confirmation﴾, after their strengthening (tashdidiha), so that you break them. ﴿And you have certainly made Allah your surety﴾, a witness to your fulfilment.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾. The scholars differed concerning who this verse was revealed about, although its ruling is general.

It was said: it was revealed concerning those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah commanded them to fulfil it [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim from Muzayyida ibn Jabir. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/161; Zad al-Masir: 4/484.]].

Mujahid and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning the alliances of the people of the Jahiliyyah [[Ibid.]].

Then Allah set forth a parable for breaking the covenant, saying: ﴿And do not be like she who unravels her yarn after it has been made strong﴾, ﴿And do not be like she who unravels her yarn after it has been made strong﴾, meaning: after its spinning and its firm twisting.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: she was a foolish, senseless woman from Quraysh, called "Rayta daughter of 'Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Ka'b ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim," and she was nicknamed "Ji'r." She had a whispering obsession (waswasa). She had made a spindle about a cubit in length, a whorl like a finger, and a large wheel suited to it, and she would spin coarse yarn from wool, hair and fleece, and she would order her maidservants to do the same. They would spin from morning until midday, and when midday came she would order them to unravel everything they had spun. This was her habit [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/531. Qatadah and Mujahid said: that is a parable struck for one who breaks his covenant after confirming it, not about a specific woman; and this is more likely and more evident, whether or not there was a woman in Makkah who unravelled her yarn. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/585; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 8/500.]].

Its meaning: she did not cease from work, and when she was working she did not cease from unravelling; likewise you, when you break the covenant, have not refrained from the covenant, nor, when you made the covenant, did you keep faith with it.

﴿Into shreds (ankathan)﴾, meaning: unravelled, its singular being "naks," which is what is unravelled after being twisted, whether yarn or rope.

﴿Taking your oaths as a means of deceit between you (dakhalan baynakum)﴾, meaning: deceit, treachery and fraud. "Dakhal" is what enters into a thing for corruption.

It was also said: "dakhal" and "daghal" mean that one displays fidelity while concealing breach.

﴿Lest one nation be more numerous (an takuna ummatun hiya arba)﴾, meaning: so that (li-an takuna), ﴿one nation be more numerous﴾, meaning: greater and higher, ﴿than another nation (min ummatin)﴾. Mujahid said: that was because they used to make alliances with allies, and when they found a people more numerous than them and mightier, they would break the alliance with these and ally themselves with the more numerous. So its meaning is: you sought honour by breaking the covenant, because one nation was more numerous than another. Thus Allah forbade them from that.

﴿Indeed, Allah tests you by it (innama yabluwkum Allahu bihi)﴾, Allah tries you by His command to you to fulfil the covenant. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ﴾ in the world.
